children: Asian markets were mostly higher on Wednesday, with Japan, China, Hong Kong, India and Australia all gaining, as investors looked ahead to the Federal Reserve’s policy decision while monitoring elevated oil prices and geopolitical tensions.
Wall Street’s major averages closed lower on Tuesday as a selloff in the bond market added pressure ahead of the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision Wednesday.
U.S. stock futures moved higher on Wednesday, with Dow futures up 0.22%, S&P 500 futures gaining 0.22% and Nasdaq futures rising 0.30%.
Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 0.51%, and the Japanese yen weakened past 155 per dollar on Wednesday, extending its decline for a third consecutive session.

params.linkText: Japan’s August trade deficit widens sharply on higher imports.

children: China’s Shanghai Composite gained 0.57%, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index advanced 0.12%.
India’s Sensex rose 0.28%. Passenger vehicle sales in India soared 33.2% Y/Y in August.

Australia’s ASX 200 gained 0.27%. The Australian dollar steadied around $0.71, near a four-week low, as a firmer U.S. dollar and higher Treasury yields weighed ahead of the Federal Reserve’s policy decision.

Gold climbed back above $4,300 an ounce on Wednesday, ending a two-session decline as gains in oil prices and bond yields lost. Crude oil fell below $105 per barrel on Wednesday, retreating from four-month highs after industry data showed a surprise increase in US crude inventories.

title: Asian markets advance ahead of Fed decision
